doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Subbing with Blood, Sweat & Tears
summary: He subbed in eight to ten gigs, learning charts sent to him, under Carl Fischer.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah. And sometimes when there’s a potential train wreck in the music it recovers nicely and it becomes like a thing.
Mistakes are good. You played, I don’t know how long before, but you played with one of my favorite bands, with Blood Sweat & Tears.
Um hum. I spent about a year.
How did you learn that music? Did they have the charts and all that?
Yeah. Were you expected to memorize them?

I was expected to get a grasp on them and be ready for the gig. Some of the other guys had sheet music on music stands. I in a lot of situations will put music onto my iPad, so and with this software where it’s for reading music off of an iPad. So I did a lot of listening, looking through the parts.
Was that with David Clayton Thomas? © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
No. He was not — this was just like around a year ago.

So I was subbing onto that band. I don’t know if I did eight or ten gigs with them. The musical director at the time was my old friend from Maynard’s band, Carl Fischer, who is now a featured trumpet player with Billy Joel. So he left his position with Blood, Sweat & Tears and he’s got plenty to do with Billy Joel and other things. But yeah, so that was — I appreciate those kind of experiences.
